summary.purpose: Help teams develop software in Bosch Corporate Design.
summary.core_requirement: Teams need a basic understanding of Core and the general design principles of the Digital Design System to fully implement the designs.

intro_content: This section helps develop software in Bosch Corporate Design . To fully implement the designs, a basic understanding of the Core and the general design principles of the Digital Design System is required: See general design principles

page_sections.title: Responsive layout grid
content: The responsive layout grid is a guide for the placement of components and elements within software . The grid adapts to the screen sizes and their alignment, ensuring a consistent appearance across differing layouts: View basic design principles

subsections.title: Structure
items: Baseline grid: All components are aligned along a square 0.5 rem (8 px) baseline grid for mobile devices, tables and desktops. This allows for easy definition of spacing between individual rows and individual sections.
Column grid: The even spacing to screen margins and between columns(gutter) must be at least 1 rem (16 px) wide. Other possible spacings can be 1.5 or 2 rem.

Column amount: The easily divisible 12-column grid allows a variation of twelve, six, four, three, two, or one evenly spaced column. Instead of using twelve columns, an amount of columns of choice can be used as design aid (i.e. five columns).

Info: As an example, the views in the components under "Responsive behaviour" are implemented in 12 columns for desktop and tablet and in four columns for mobile. In this way, the display remains consistent throughout the entire digital design system.Alternative column numbers for implementation are available in the Sketch file. The component definitions are based on the 12 column grid.

subsections.title: Break points
items: Break points help display components correctly on every device and in any size. As a result, the width of a container is defined by the active break point.
*Margin and gutters are flexible in size and can equal 1, 1.5 or 2 rem.
**The Side Navigation is offset to the baseline grid. The left margin equals 80 px when the Side Navigation is closed, and 288 px when opened.

subsections.title: Text sizes and line spacing
items: The font sizes and line spacing are generally defined in rem and are predefined in Core .

page_sections.title: Spacings
content: The Bosch Digital Design System offers predefined spacing within the components and – for the layout process – between the components:
More on general spacing

page_sections.title: Page structure
content: Pages can be structured through use of Dividers or different background colors. The type of structure depends on the amount and structure of the content.
Simple structure on a Primary Background:
The content is placed on a Primary Background .
The Primary Background is generally used for simple content.
Dividers can be used on long pages as structural element. However, Dividers may not be combined with tables on a page.
Strong structuring based on surfaces with differing colors This design principle is done using the Card component .
The content can be placed on the Card as well as the (grey) Secondary Background . The allocation of content must be reasonable and logical.
This is used on long pages with complex content, i.e. when multiple tables or forms are consecutive.

page_sections.title: Message types
content: Feedback can be provided via messages. These have three different priorities:
Low priority:
Toast
A Toast is shown temporarily, and fades away independently and without needing user interaction.
It does not contain a Close Button.
The content can, for example, inform users of a successful interaction (i.e. data was saved).
Medium priority: Notification (Core)
A Notification informs users of successful actions taken.
Can display further information via Text Links .
It can contain a Close Button.
The content can, for example, inform users of correct or incorrect input.
High priority: Dialog (Core)
The Dialog requires user input via CTA.
Can contain a Close Button.
The content can, for example, trigger the process of an interaction via confirmation (i.e. delete).

page_sections.title: References
content: Please submit all feature requests and bug reports relating to the Digital Design System or the Frontend Kit directly to the digital expert team via Jira. You can learn more about how the process works, here .
If you have any feedback or questions about designing digital touchpoints, feel free to send them to support.design@bosch.com . We’re also happy to check design drafts.
